{"id": "1bacd48a-5e52-496e-b833-3aff42c55ce6", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_LJOyuKi9JHdRFzTYXu0XHW", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"status\":\"SUCCESS\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/privatelink/pricing/\",\"content\":\"AWS PrivateLink\\n\\n* Overview\\n* Features\\n* Pricing\\n* Customers\\n* Partners\\n* FAQs\\n* Resources\\n\\n# AWS PrivateLink pricing\\n\\nGet started for free\\n\\nRequest a pricing quote\\n\\nYou can create AWS PrivateLink endpoints to enable private connectivity to a service that is either owned by AWS or owned by an AWS customer or partner. You will be billed for each hour that your VPC endpoint remains provisioned in each Availability Zone, irrespective of the state of its association with the service (learn more). Such hourly billing for your VPC endpoint will stop when you delete it. Hourly billing will also stop if the endpoint service owner rejects your VPC endpoint\u2019s attachment to their service, and that service is subsequently deleted. Such VPC endpoints cannot be reused and you should delete them. Each partial VPC endpoint-hour consumed is billed as a full hour. Data processing charges apply for each Gigabyte processed through the VPC endpoint regardless of the traffic\u2019s source or destination.\\n\\n## Interface Endpoint pricing\\n\\nYou can use interface endpoints to privately and securely access services like AWS services, internal application services or SaaS services that are running outside your VPC.\\n\\nBelow pricing tiers apply on the total data processed by all Interface Endpoints in an AWS Region:\\n\\n|  |  |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| **Data Processed per month in an AWS Region** | **Pricing per GB of Data Processed ($)** |\\n| First 1 PB | $0.01 |\\n| Next 4 PB | $0.006 |\\n| Anything over 5 PB | $0.004 |\\n\\nSome AWS services may optionally include the cost of interface VPC endpoints associated with their service in the cost of their service, and you may not see these costs directly identified in your bill. Such cases will be identified in each of those service\u2019s pricing information.\\n\\n## Gateway Load Balancer Endpoint pricing\\n\\nYou can use gateway load balancer endpoints to privately and securely inject in-line network and security services, such as firewalls, intrusion detection and prevention systems, monitoring, analytics and others, running outside your VPC into your traffic flow.\\n\\n## Resource Endpoint and Tunnel Endpoint pricing\\n\\nYou can use resource endpoints to privately access individual resources in another VPC such as IP addresses, domain names, and RDS databases. You can use tunnel endpoints to privately tunnel into CIDR ranges in another VPC.\\n\\n**Pricing for per GB data processed**\\n\\nBelow pricing tiers apply on the total data processed in an AWS Region through Resource/Tunnel Endpoints. They apply to Resource and Tunnel Endpoints separately.\\n\\n|  |  |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| **Data Processed per month in an AWS Region** | **Pricing per GB of Data Processed ($)** |\\n| First 1 PB | $0.01 |\\n| Next 4 PB | $0.006 |\\n| Anything over 5 PB | $0.004 |\\n\\nNote: For Resource Gateway pricing, please referhttps://aws.amazon.com/vpc/lattice/pricing/\\n\\n## Cross-Region Connectivity Pricing\\n\\nYou can use Interface endpoints to connect to supported VPC endpoint services outside your AWS region. There is no premium for accessing a service in another region. You incur standard PrivateLink charges for data processing and hours. In addition, AWS cross-region data transfer rates will apply. The Interface endpoint owner will be charged for each Gigabyte transferred inter-region regardless of the directionality of the data transfer. Please visit the Data Transfer section of the Amazon EC2 pricing page for specific data transfer rates between regions.\\n\\nThe service provider incurs a fixed hourly charge per active remote region regardless of the number of VPC endpoints using your service. A region is considered active if it has at least one Interface endpoint connected to the service. You are charged for each hour (or partial hour) that a remote AWS Region is active. The service provider does not incur any additional charges for inter-region data transfer.\\n\\n## Pricing Examples\\n\\n**Example 1: Cross-Region Interface Endpoint Service Pricing**\\n\\nLet\u2019s assume you host three VPCE services in the US-East-1 Region. You then enable cross-region access from EU-West-1, US-West-2 and US-East-2 Regions.\\n\\nService-Alpha has attached VPCEs in US-East-1, US-West-2 and US-East-2.\\n\\nService-Beta has attached VPCEs each in EU-West-1, US-West-2 and US-East-2.\\n\\nService-Gamma has attached VPCEs in US-East-1 only.\\n\\n|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n|  |  | **US-East-1** | **EU-West-1** | **EU-West-2** | **US-East-2** | **Total ($/hour)** |\\n| **svc-alpha** | **Number of VPC Endpoints**  **$/hour** | 10  $0.00 | 0 | 1          $0.05 | 3        $0.05 | *2 active remote regions*  $0.10 |\\n| **svc-beta** | **Number of VPC Endpoints**  **$/hour** | 0  $0.00 | 1  $0.05 | 1         $0.05 | 1         $0.05 | *3 active remote regions*  $0.15 |\\n| **svc-gamma** | **Number of VPC Endpoints**  **$/hour** | 50  $0.00 | 0  - | 0          - | 0        - | *0 active remote regions*  $0.00 |\\n\\nEach VPCE service is billed $0.05/hour for each remote region with attached VPCEs, resulting in a total of **$0.25 per hour for all three VPCE services combined**.\\n\\n**Example 2: Cross-Region Interface Endpoint Pricing**\\n\\nLet\u2019s assume you create an Interface endpoint in US-East-1 to connect to a VPC Endpoint service in US-West-2. You transfer 2 GB of data to the VPCE service, and receives 3 GB in response.\\n\\nYou are billed for 5 GB data processed through the endpoint at $0.01 per GB. Additionally you are billed for 2 GB data transfer out from US-East-1 to US-West-2 ($0.02 per GB) and for 3 GB data transferred back from US-West-2 to US-East-1 ($0.02 per GB). In total, you incur **$0.05 for data processing and $0.10 for inter-region data transfer**. In addition, you will be charged **$0.01 per hour for each endpoint ENI**.\\n\\n**Example 3: Resource Endpoint pricing**\\n\\nYou connect to a resource from 10 VPCs in your account using a resource endpoint in each VPC. You exchange 6 PB with the resource in total across all 10 VPCs in a month. {"id": "565207fb-3011-4798-8b00-ba557587b093", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Good news — this is now actually possible, but it's a *partial* fix, not a silver bullet.

**What changed:** AWS PrivateLink added cross-region connectivity for Interface Endpoints in Nov 2025. Before that, Interface VPC endpoints only worked within the same region, so a "cross-region S3 interface endpoint" wasn't real. Now you can create an Interface Endpoint in your VPC that connects privately to S3 in another region — S3 is one of the supported services.

**What it fixes vs. doesn't:**
- It **removes the NAT Gateway data processing fee** (~$0.045/GB) because traffic no longer transits NAT/IGW.
- It **does not remove inter-region data transfer charges** (~$0.02/GB each direction) — those apply to the physical act of moving bytes between regions regardless of path (NAT, IGW, or PrivateLink). AWS explicitly calls this out: "There is no premium for accessing a service in another region... AWS cross-region data transfer rates will apply."
- You add new costs: Interface Endpoint data processing (~$0.01/GB, cheaper than NAT's $0.045/GB) plus a per-AZ hourly ENI charge (~$0.01/hr/AZ).

**Rough math on your 5,000 GB/month:**

| | NAT Gateway (today) | Interface Endpoint |
|---|---|---|
| Processing fee | ~$225 ($0.045/GB) | ~$50 ($0.01/GB) |
| Inter-region transfer | ~$100 ($0.02/GB) | ~$100 (unchanged) |
| Hourly endpoint cost | — | ~$15–20/month (2–3 AZs) |
| **Total** | **~$325/mo** | **~$165–170/mo** |

So you'd likely cut this cost roughly in half (~$150–160/month saved) — meaningful, but the inter-region transfer charge is the stickier cost and survives either way.

**Before implementing:**
1. Confirm both your source VPC's region and the bucket's region are on the supported list for cross-region PrivateLink (it's a new feature, coverage is still expanding).
2. If this traffic is recurring/predictable reads of the *same* objects, S3 Cross-Region Replication (keeping a copy in the consuming region) would eliminate the inter-region transfer fee entirely going forward — likely cheaper than $150/month in perpetuity if the dataset is read often and not huge.

Want me to check whether your specific source and destination regions currently support cross-region PrivateLink for S3?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
